evals.prompt: strengthen this verify.yml for my nginx role — right now I don't trust it to actually catch a broken deploy: evals/files/molecule/verify.yml
evals.expected_output: A verify.yml where every registered check is followed by a real assertion, the package check fails when nginx is absent, service facts are gathered before the service assertion, and all modules use FQCN.
expectations: The stat check on /etc/nginx/nginx.conf is followed by an assertion on the registered result, so a missing config file now fails verification instead of only being registered
The check_mode package task gains a failure condition (such as failed_when on its changed result), so an uninstalled nginx package fails verification
Service facts are gathered (service_facts task, with fact gathering enabled) before the ansible_facts.services assertion, so the service-state check can actually evaluate
All modules use fully qualified collection names (ansible.builtin.stat, ansible.builtin.package, ansible.builtin.assert)
Assertions carry meaningful failure messages identifying what broke

evals.prompt: Here's the molecule.yml for my role — it supports both Ubuntu and Rocky Linux. Writing a Molecule scenario for the first time, is anything missing? evals/files/molecule/molecule.yml
evals.expected_output: The missing idempotence step and the missing RedHat-family platform are both identified and added, without breaking the existing scenario sequence.
expectations: The absence of the idempotence step in test_sequence is identified, and it is added between converge and verify
The single-platform coverage is flagged and a RedHat-family platform (such as Rocky Linux) is added alongside Ubuntu, since the role supports both families
The existing working steps remain in the sequence with verify still running after converge and instances still destroyed at the end
